clue.text: Frantic doctor nurses English XI and German XI

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, as in nursing a drink, so the doctor's name holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: Bones is the nickname of Dr McCoy in Star Trek
a cricket or football XI is a side, a team of eleven
elf is the German word for eleven

explanation.surface: A doctor in a panic looks after two eleven-man teams, one English and one German.
explanation.walkthrough: The two XIs are treated differently: the English one is a team (SIDE), the German one is the number eleven in German (ELF).
explanation.definitionFit: Being frantic means being out of your mind with worry or agitation, the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Tramp keeps jazzy shirt, I think, for tourist site

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so the vagrant's word contains the rest

parts.note: bum is slang for a tramp or vagrant

indicators.note: jazzy means flashy and lively, so these letters are jazzed up into a new order

parts.note: to muse is to think or ponder

explanation.surface: A vagrant hangs on to a loud shirt for a visit to a London attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: The national museum in Bloomsbury, London, is one of the city's most visited attractions.

clue.text: One takes off clothes, turning brown

indicators.note: turning round, so the whole thing is read backwards
to clothe is to cover, so the verb surrounds the numeral

parts.note: to take off someone is to mimic them, to ape
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A stripper gets a tan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes off clothes' reads as undressing; 'clothes' is in fact a verb, wrapping APES around I to make APIES, which turns into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown colour, originally a pigment from cuttlefish ink.

clue.text: Hairy and desperate chap rogues manhandled

parts.note: Desperate Dan is the strongman of the British comic The Dandy

indicators.note: roughly handled, so these letters are pushed about into a new order

explanation.surface: A hairy, desperate man is roughed up by villains.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan, a stubbly cowboy in a long-running British children's comic, gives DAN. 'Hairy' is informal for risky.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairy is colloquial for frighteningly risky, as in a hairy moment on the road.

clue.text: See 1
Exploding cigar no good for one's health?

indicators.note: something exploding is blown apart, so these letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A trick exploding cigar is hardly a healthy thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no good' looks like a phrase, but 'no' is fodder and 'good' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic food, grown without synthetic chemicals, is marketed as healthier, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Biblical character and husband shape up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a cone is a geometric shape

explanation.surface: A Bible figure and her husband get fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Enoch is an Old Testament patriarch, father of Methuselah, said to have walked with God.

clue.text: People about to tour country in vehicle

indicators.note: to tour is to go round, so the reversed word goes round the nation
about means turned round, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: a race is a people
a state is a country

explanation.surface: Folk are set to travel round a nation by car.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate car is the British name for a station wagon, a type of motor vehicle.

clue.text: They prevent issue in Norman Mailer's writings?

parts.note: the Normans spoke French, so Norman can mean French
the writings of a mailer, someone who posts things, are letters

explanation.surface: A question about what lies in the novels of the American writer Norman Mailer.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman Mailer the novelist splits into Norman (French) and mailer (one who posts). 'Issue' means offspring; the answer is old British slang for condoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Condoms are contraceptives, preventing pregnancy and so offspring, which is the legal sense of issue.

clue.text: Dutch or transatlantic pageant winner

definitions.meaning: in Cockney slang, my old Dutch is my wife
the beauty queen crowned in the American pageant, read as two words

explanation.surface: A choice between a Netherlander and an American beauty queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch here is Cockney slang for a wife, from duchess, not a nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Missus is informal for a wife, and split it gives the title of the US beauty queen.

clue.text: Terror about to finish soon

parts.note: a little terror is a naughty child, an imp
something ending is about to finish

explanation.surface: A frightening episode is about to be over soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to finish' looks like it belongs with the definition, but it is the second piece; 'soon' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An impending event is one coming soon, about to happen in the near future.

clue.text: Bizarre journey, moving right to the east

indicators.note: the right letter is shifted from its place in the journey word
in an across clue east is rightwards, so the letter goes to the end

parts.note: a route is the way taken on a journey

explanation.surface: A strange trip in which someone keeps heading east.
explanation.walkthrough: ROUTE has its R taken from the front and put at the right-hand end.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré is a French borrowing for unconventional or eccentric, a synonym of bizarre.

clue.text: That is skirting issue still

indicators.note: to skirt is to go round the edge, so the two letters sit either side

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is
an issue of a periodical is a mag, short for magazine

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark that a matter remains unresolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like an adverb but is the noun: a single frame from a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a photograph or single frame from a film, so it is a picture.

clue.text: Tiny chest, bust that's fake

indicators.note: something bust is broken, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A small chest and a bust revealed as not genuine, as with cosmetic surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' plays on the chest theme but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synthetic means artificial or man-made rather than natural, hence not genuine.

clue.text: Boy digs into brownies and plum, being offered nothing else

indicators.note: the boy burrows inside the word for the sprites

parts.note: brownies are household sprites, and a hob is a hobgoblin or such sprite
a son is a boy
a plum job is a choice one, the pick

explanation.surface: A boy tucks into chocolate brownies and a plum, with nothing else on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: Brownies here are sprites, not cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a choice that is no choice at all: take what is offered or nothing.

clue.text: New York girl group makes fast connection

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman
a band is a musical group

explanation.surface: An American girl band makes a quick link.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadband is high-speed internet access, so it is a quick link to the web.

clue.text: See 13
Released song that's top in terms of quantity

parts.note: a record that is out has been released
a number is a song in a performance

explanation.surface: A newly released track goes straight to the top of the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed in count is to be more numerous, beating another side on sheer numbers.

clue.text: Solve problem about right back

indicators.note: the phrase goes around the next letter

parts.note: to solve a maths problem is to do a sum

explanation.surface: An instruction to work out a sum concerning the right-back in football.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right back' looks like a football position; the two words split.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorsum is the anatomical Latin term for the back or upper surface of a body part.

clue.text: Reversal of space-time where craft are made fast

indicators.note: the word for space is turned backwards

parts.note: room means space
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A physics conundrum about reversing space-time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'space-time' reads as physics; only 'space' is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A mooring place is where boats are tied up securely, made fast in the nautical sense.

clue.text: A learner follows more advanced kind of thinking

indicators.note: a and learner come after the comparative in the answer

parts.note: later means further on, more advanced in time
L is the learner plate letter

explanation.surface: A student pursues a more advanced type of reasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral thinking is the idiom for solving problems by indirect, creative approaches.

clue.text: Indicator of base books with lots of mawkishness

parts.note: lit is short for literature, books

indicators.note: lots of, but not all, means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: mush is sentimental slush, mawkishness

explanation.surface: A sign of low quality: books dripping with sentimentality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like low or vile, but it is the chemical alkali.
explanation.definitionFit: Litmus paper turns blue in alkaline solutions, so it detects an alkali in chemistry.

clue.text: See 7
See 1
Scots remarkable at comprehending the German primer

indicators.note: to comprehend is to include, so the article is held inside

parts.note: unco is a Scots word meaning remarkable or extraordinary
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Scots, impressively, take in a German beginner's book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primer' looks like a first reading book, but it is the paint.
explanation.definitionFit: A primer is the first coat of paint, applied beneath the topcoat as a base layer.

clue.text: Set that's endless — one spoke and spoke

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a radio is a wireless set
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A broadcaster talking on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoke and spoke' looks like a verb repeated, but it is two of the noun: wheel spokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Radii is the plural of radius, lines from centre to rim, like wheel spokes.

clue.text: University teachers admitting middling grade is rough

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the grade goes inside

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union
C is a middling exam grade, between A and E

explanation.surface: University staff concede an average mark is a bit rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' is the sense of an uncut, unpolished gem.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncut diamond is a rough one, in its natural unworked state.

clue.text: Schoolchildren maybe working

definitions.meaning: pupils taught together in one group, the maybe because they are just an example
the word that comes before in the name of the social stratum of manual labourers

explanation.surface: Pupils perhaps getting down to work.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a prompt: working precedes the answer in the name of a social group.
explanation.definitionFit: A school form is a group of pupils, and the working ranks of society form one social stratum.

clue.text: African native's internet domain?

parts.note: e- is the internet prefix, as in e-mail
a domain is a realm or land

explanation.surface: A question about an African's website address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'internet domain' looks like a single web term; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large antelope found in African grasslands, so it is native there.

clue.text: A silly price for sketch

parts.note: dumb means silly or stupid
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: A daft amount charged for a drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: To adumbrate is to outline or represent in faint, partial form, as a drawn outline would.

clue.text: Goddess on film cried sadly, desiring lost youth

indicators.note: in an across clue the goddess comes on, after, the other piece
sadly suggests things gone wrong, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: Isis is the Egyptian goddess

explanation.surface: A goddess weeps over a film that makes her long for her youth.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the anxious stage in middle age when people yearn for their younger years.
